intervention_label: KRAS G12R allele biology (target-feature mechanism; not a single agent)
model_system: human PDAC cell lines carrying KRAS G12R vs G12D/G12V; biochemical p110alpha binding and macropinocytosis assays
control_arm: isogenic and allele-matched KRAS G12D/G12V PDAC lines
mechanism: Switch II is structurally perturbed in G12R, so the mutant binds the p110alpha catalytic subunit of PI3K poorly and cannot drive PI3K-dependent macropinocytosis the way G12D and G12V do; PDAC cells compensate with KRAS-independent PI3Kgamma acting through RAC1.
key_finding: G12R lines did not run KRAS-driven macropinocytosis and did not require MYC for it, unlike G12D/V lines. The compensating nutrient-uptake route ran through PI3Kgamma rather than KRAS. Drug-sensitivity profiles separated G12R from G12D lines, though both stayed responsive to combined ERK and autophagy inhibition.
caveats: Cell-line and biochemical work with no in-vivo arm. Nothing here tests whether a pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor engages G12R with the same potency it engages G12D.

intervention_label: KRAS G12R allele biology (target-feature mechanism; not a single agent)
model_system: KrasLSL-G12R/+;Trp53LSL-R172H/+;p48Cre-ER GEMM; murine and human PDAC cell lines; PDX models; human PDAC tissue
control_arm: KrasG12D GEMM and G12D-mutant human lines/PDX
mechanism: G12R produces less nuclear ERK/MAPK translocation and therefore weaker transcriptional output than G12D, and direct KRAS-driven PI3K activation is what the mouse model needs for efficient tumor initiation.
key_finding: Only about 10% of KrasG12R;Trp53R172H mice formed pancreatic tumors within a year, against rapid multifocal disease in G12D animals. Both alleles switched on the same pancreas-specific transcriptional network, but G12R did so weakly. Human G12R tumors carried less collagen deposition and less metastatic liver invasion.
caveats: The mouse p53 allele is R172H, so the co-mutation is analogous to this patient's Y220C rather than matched. Reduced collagen in human G12R tumors cuts against the desmoplastic-barrier story for this allele, but that part is an association in tissue, not an intervention.

intervention_label: KRAS G12R allele biology (target-feature mechanism; not a single agent)
model_system: Ptf1a-tdTomato lineage-tracing mice expressing different KRAS mutants, with genetic, pharmacologic and inflammatory perturbation in vivo
control_arm: KRAS G12D mice under the same perturbations
mechanism: G12R and G12V fail to raise EGFR, AKT and RAC1/VAV1 signalling enough to license acinar-to-ductal lineage reversion and the accompanying enhancer reprogramming at Pou2f3 and Vav1.
key_finding: G12D co-opted pancreatic injury to drive dedifferentiation and tumor initiation, while G12R and G12V could not sustain the dedifferentiated transcriptional or chromatin programs. Constitutive AKT activation was sufficient to rescue G12R tumorigenic potential in vivo.
caveats: Tumor-initiation biology in mice, not treatment of established disease. Its therapeutic reading is indirect: an allele that leans on AKT to get started may not behave like G12D under MAPK-directed pressure.

intervention_label: KRAS G12R-selective covalent chemistry (no clinical agent exists)
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
model_system: recombinant K-Ras(G12R) protein; X-ray crystallography of the ligand-protein adduct
mechanism: alpha,beta-diketoamide electrophiles bind the switch II pocket and condense irreversibly with the epsilon- and eta-nitrogens of arginine 12, forming an imidazolium adduct.
key_finding: Allele-selective covalent ligation of G12R was achieved and confirmed structurally, showing that a weakly nucleophilic arginine can be targeted at all. No cellular potency, pathway-suppression, or animal data accompany the chemistry.
caveats: Chemistry proof of concept only. Four years on, no G12R-selective inhibitor has entered the clinic, which is the honest bound on this route for this patient.

intervention_label: ERK plus autophagy inhibition (allele-linked vulnerability; no surfaced trial)
model_system: PDAC cell lines and patient-derived xenografts; NRAS-mutant melanoma and BRAF-mutant CRC PDX for breadth
control_arm: single-agent trametinib and single-agent chloroquine
dose_and_schedule: trametinib plus chloroquine, doses per published xenograft protocol
mechanism: MEK1/2 blockade activates the LKB1-AMPK-ULK1 axis and the resulting autophagy buffers cells against loss of KRAS pathway output; blocking autophagy removes the buffer.
key_finding: Trametinib plus chloroquine was synergistic in vitro and regressed patient-derived PDAC xenografts where neither agent alone did. A patient treated with trametinib plus hydroxychloroquine had a partial response.
caveats: No G12R-specific arm; the allele link comes from Hobbs 2020, which reports G12R lines retain sensitivity to combined ERK/autophagy inhibition. No trial surfaced for this case uses this combination.

intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) / RMC-7977 tool analogue, pan-RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor
model_system: RAS-addicted human cancer cell lines and xenografts across RAS genotypes, weighted to KRAS codon-12 mutants
control_arm: vehicle; KRAS G12C(OFF) inhibitor comparison in G12C-resistant models
mechanism: RMC-7977 assembles a tri-complex with cyclophilin A and the GTP-bound (ON) state of KRAS, NRAS and HRAS, sterically blocking effector engagement by mutant and wild-type RAS simultaneously.
key_finding: Tumor regression at tolerated exposures across RAS-addicted models, deepest in KRAS codon-12 mutants. Models that had escaped G12C(OFF) inhibitors by restoring RAS pathway signalling remained sensitive.
caveats: RMC-7977 is the tool analogue of the clinical agent. Activity is reported for KRAS G12X in aggregate with no G12R-specific arm, which is the gap the whole clinical estimand for this patient inherits.

intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) / RMC-7977 tool analogue, pan-RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor
model_system: autochthonous KPC mice, PDAC organoids and cell lines, xenografts
control_arm: vehicle-treated KPC and xenograft cohorts; normal tissue used as the selectivity comparator
mechanism: Broad RAS-GTP inhibition collapses tumor RAS output while normal epithelium tolerates it, so tumors take waves of apoptosis plus sustained proliferative arrest and normal tissue only slows transiently.
key_finding: Anti-tumor activity was broad across PDAC models at well-tolerated exposures. KPC survival was extended substantially before on-treatment relapse, and relapsed tumors were enriched for Myc copy gain, which TEAD inhibition countered in vitro.
caveats: KPC is Kras G12D-driven, so allele transfer to G12R is an assumption rather than a result. An author correction was issued in 2024 (PMID 39533066) without altering the conclusions.

intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, pan-RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor) — acquired resistance
model_system: human and murine PDAC preclinical models, anchored to paired pretreatment/end-of-treatment ctDNA from 44 phase 1/2 patients
n_units: 44 paired ctDNA samples; model arms not enumerated in the abstract
mechanism: Escape restores RAS pathway signalling rather than altering the drug site: mutant KRAS amplification, MYC amplification, and receptor tyrosine kinase upregulation.
key_finding: RAS-pathway alterations emerged in 26 of 44 patients and mutant KRAS amplification in 16 of 44, with no secondary KRAS mutations at all, unlike the G12C(OFF) resistance pattern. Pairing daraxonrasib with DNA-damage-response agents, RTK inhibitors, or zoldonrasib averted resistance in models.
caveats: Cohort is RAS-mutant PDAC broadly, with no G12R breakdown. The zoldonrasib pairing is G12D-directed and does not transfer to this tumor.

intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) — allele-specific resistance in KRAS G12R
model_system: KRAS G12R vs G12D PDAC cell lines; 3D-bioprinted patient-derived toroids; one G12R patient's tumor tissue
control_arm: KRAS G12D lines under matched daraxonrasib pressure
mechanism: G12R cannot transactivate wild-type RAS, so daraxonrasib-adapted G12R cells lean on EGFR-driven wild-type RAS-GTP, while G12D cells retain mutant KRAS-GTP signalling with reduced cyclophilin A, the partner daraxonrasib needs.
key_finding: The shift to EGFR/RAS-WT in resistant G12R cells conferred trametinib sensitivity, which the bioprinted toroid model reproduced. A G12R patient who progressed after 10 months on daraxonrasib showed intratumoral EGFR/RAS-WT activation and got roughly 5 months of control on sixth-line trametinib-based therapy.
caveats: bioRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed, with a single-patient clinical anchor. Read it as a hypothesis about what follows daraxonrasib in a G12R tumor, not as established resistance biology.

intervention_label: daraxonrasib / zoldonrasib resistance via CDK8-driven microenvironment remodeling
model_system: PDAC mouse models profiled by spatial transcriptomics, scRNA-seq and CODEX; PDX resistant to daraxonrasib and to zoldonrasib
control_arm: vehicle and single-agent MRTX1133 arms; anti-CTLA-4 alone
mechanism: CDK8 induces CXCL2 secretion and suppresses FAS expression, remodeling the microenvironment toward immune evasion after the initial T-cell influx that KRAS inhibition produces.
key_finding: MRTX1133 first raised CD11c+ and T-cell infiltration near cancer cells, then that response reversed as CDK8-dependent resistance took hold. Targeting CDK8, alone or with anti-CTLA-4, overcame resistance, and CDK8 was also upregulated in daraxonrasib- and zoldonrasib-resistant PDX.
caveats: The primary models are G12D-driven; the daraxonrasib link rests on the PDX arm. No CDK8 inhibitor appears among the interventions surfaced for this case.

intervention_label: KRAS-pathway inhibition and immune remodeling in PDAC (MRTX1133 as tool compound)
model_system: 16 KRAS G12D-driven PDAC mouse models plus human patient-derived organoids
control_arm: vehicle; CD8 depletion arm; checkpoint blockade alone
mechanism: Blocking mutant KRAS induces FAS on cancer cells and shifts the microenvironment — more CD8+ effectors, fewer myeloid cells, reprogrammed CAFs — so CD8+ T cells can kill through FAS/FASL.
key_finding: MRTX1133 regressed both established PanIN and advanced PDAC, and regression of advanced disease depended on CD8+ T cells. Checkpoint blockade synergized with it and extended survival.
caveats: The tool compound is G12D-selective, and whether pan-RAS(ON) inhibition produces the same immune switch in a G12R tumor with lower ERK output is untested. Still the strongest mechanistic argument that anything in the surfaced set could open an MSS, TMB-low pancreatic tumor to T cells.

intervention_label: ELI-002 amphiphile vaccine platform (lymph-node-targeted mKRAS peptide + CpG)
model_system: murine syngeneic solid-tumor models with adoptive TCR-T transfer; human TCR-T in vitro against NY-ESO-1, mutant KRAS and HPV16 E7
control_arm: TCR-T monotherapy; unvaccinated controls
mechanism: Amphiphile conjugation traffics peptide and CpG adjuvant into draining lymph nodes, maturing antigen-presenting cells and expanding both transferred and endogenous antigen-specific T cells without lymphodepletion.
key_finding: Vaccine plus TCR-T eradicated established tumors that resisted TCR-T alone, with durable protection and antigen spreading to antigens outside the vaccine. Matched amphiphile peptides improved proliferation, activation and cytotoxicity of human mutant-KRAS TCR-T in vitro.
caveats: Not a PDAC model and no G12R-specific in-vivo arm, though the clinical peptide pool covers that allele. Platforms of this class were built for low tumor burden, which a growing radiographic recurrence is not.

intervention_label: rezatapopt (PC14586, p53 Y220C reactivator)
model_system: Y220C-mutant human tumor cell lines and xenografts; biochemical and structural analysis; in vitro and in vivo transcriptomics
control_arm: vehicle; p53 wild-type and non-Y220C mutant lines
mechanism: The compound occupies the crevice the Y220C substitution creates, correcting the fold of the DNA-binding domain so p53 binds DNA and drives its wild-type target program again.
key_finding: Multiple arms of the wild-type p53 program were recovered in cells and in tumors, with antiproliferative effect. Antitumor activity held as monotherapy and improved in combination with immunotherapy.
caveats: No PDAC model and no KRAS-mutant background is reported, which is precisely the gap the clinical KRAS-wild-type responder pattern points at.

intervention_label: rezatapopt (PC14586, p53 Y220C reactivator) — stability-response relationship
model_system: recombinant p53 Y220C/Y220N/Y220S proteins with high-resolution crystal structures; matched mutant-expressing cell lines
control_arm: wild-type p53 stability reference; untreated mutant lines
mechanism: Nanomolar binding into the mutation-induced crevice restores near-wild-type thermal stability, and how much stability comes back sets whether the cellular p53 program returns.
key_finding: Rezatapopt restored the folded conformation, target-gene transcription, antiproliferative effect and apoptosis in Y220C cells, and in Y220S cells at higher concentrations. Y220N bound the drug with high-nanomolar affinity yet stayed too destabilized to respond, separating binding from functional rescue.
caveats: Biophysics and cell lines only — no tumor model, no KRAS co-mutation arm, no PDAC context. Its value here is that Y220C specifically is the variant with full stability rescue.

intervention_label: rezatapopt (PC14586) — on-target acquired resistance
model_system: functional modeling of engineered TP53 double mutants, anchored to patient ctDNA, biopsies and rapid-autopsy specimens at progression
control_arm: Y220C single-mutant constructs
mechanism: Second TP53 alterations arising in cis with Y220C either abolish transcriptional activity outright or reshape the drug-binding surface so rezatapopt no longer engages.
key_finding: Progression on rezatapopt was accompanied by heterogeneous secondary TP53 alterations in cis with Y220C. Engineered double mutants showed neither p53 reactivation nor target-gene induction on drug.
caveats: Resistance is on-target and heterogeneous, so a second-generation Y220C reactivator would likely inherit much of it. The specimens are clinical; only the double-mutant modeling is preclinical.

intervention_label: p53 restoration in a KRAS-driven tumor: apoptotic priming as the gate
model_system: Kras-driven p53-restorable mouse lung adenocarcinoma and sarcoma lines versus lymphoma lines; in vitro and in vivo
control_arm: lymphoma lines (high priming); BCL-2/BCL-XL overexpression and deletion arms
dose_and_schedule: navitoclax co-treatment at doses per the published protocol; p53 restored genetically rather than pharmacologically
mechanism: Whether restored p53 kills or merely arrests is set by mitochondrial apoptotic priming — how much reserve anti-apoptotic capacity the cell holds before p53 comes back.
key_finding: KRAS-driven solid-tumor lines with low priming survived p53 restoration and arrested in the cell cycle, while high-priming lymphoma cells died. Forced BCL-2/BCL-XL expression converted lymphoma to arrest, and navitoclax or BAD overexpression converted the solid-tumor lines to apoptosis in vitro and in vivo.
caveats: Genetic p53 restoration in lung and sarcoma models, not pharmacologic Y220C reactivation in PDAC. It is nonetheless the best mechanistic account available for why a KRAS-mutant tumor may arrest rather than die when p53 function returns, and it names BH3 mimetics as the in-principle rescue.

intervention_label: RAS inhibition raising p53 output (rationale for pairing pan-RAS with a Y220C reactivator)
model_system: human colon carcinoma cell lines treated with a Ras inhibitor
control_arm: untreated cells
mechanism: Cutting Ras signalling raises p53 transcription and lowers Mdm2, so p53 protein escapes degradation and gains activity through two cooperating routes.
key_finding: Ras inhibition increased p53 transcriptional activation and reduced Mdm2 in colon carcinoma cells, with the two effects additive on p53 function.
caveats: Twenty-year-old work in colon lines with wild-type p53 and pre-tri-complex Ras chemistry. It gives a direction for pairing RAS(ON) inhibition with Y220C reactivation, not evidence for that combination.

intervention_label: KMT2C/COMPASS-complex loss (target-feature mechanism; no directed agent exists)
model_system: conditional Kmt2c/Kmt2d knockout gastric GEMM, with and without Pten deletion; scRNA-seq integrated with human gastric cancer datasets
control_arm: Kmt2c/d wild-type littermates; single-agent mTORC1 inhibition and anti-PD-1 arms
mechanism: COMPASS-family loss reduces protein synthesis while raising ribosomal-protein transcription, leaving cells dependent on mTORC1; the same loss raises MHC class I and antigen presentation.
key_finding: Kmt2c/d loss with Pten deletion produced muscle-invasive gastric adenocarcinoma within three weeks of Cre induction. Knockout cells were hypersensitive to mTORC1 inhibitors, and mTORC1 inhibition plus anti-PD-1 markedly suppressed tumors in immunocompetent mice.
caveats: Gastric lineage, double Kmt2c/d knockout, and Pten co-deletion — three departures from a single KMT2C S2816fs in MSS PDAC. No KMT2C-directed agent or basket trial exists, so this stays a hypothesis rather than a route for this patient.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 as a target: lineage restriction and ectopic activation
model_system: normal and tumor tissue panels across sites; CLDN18.2-specific monoclonal antibodies tested on cancer-cell surfaces
mechanism: CLDN18.2 is a gastric-lineage tight-junction isoform whose expression depends on CREB binding an unmethylated consensus site; in normal tissue it is confined to differentiated gastric mucosa and spares the stem-cell zone.
key_finding: Ectopic CLDN18.2 activation was found in pancreatic, esophageal, ovarian and lung tumors. Antibodies were raised that bind the isoform on cancer-cell surfaces without cross-reacting with the lung splice variant CLDN18.1.
caveats: Target-discovery paper rather than an efficacy study. The normal gastric expression it documents is the on-target off-tumor liability every modality in this file carries.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 expression in pancreatic neoplasms, primaries and metastases
model_system: human pancreatic specimens: 24 normal, 202 primary lesions, 84 metastases, 48 intra-individually matched pairs; standardized IHC scored by two raters
n_units: n=202 primaries, n=84 metastases, n=48 matched pairs
mechanism: Descriptive IHC mapping of CLDN18.2 across pancreatic tumor types and their metastatic sites.
key_finding: 103 primary PDAC samples (59.2%) stained positive and 95 (54.6%) at intensity 2+ or above. Metastases were positive at comparable rates — 69.4% of nodal and 65.7% of liver lesions — so expression persisted at metastatic sites.
caveats: Pre-dates the 43-14A companion assay and the 75%-of-cells cutoff, so positivity rates are not directly comparable to a CDx call. No treatment arm.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 concordance across biopsy, resection and recurrent PDAC specimens (clone 43-14A)
model_system: human PDAC tissue: 211 resections, 133 matched preoperative biopsies, 60 recurrent-lesion samples, all stained with the trial-validated 43-14A clone
n_units: n=211 resections; n=133 matched biopsies; n=60 recurrent lesions
mechanism: Compares the same validated assay across specimen types to test whether an archival call transfers to a later or smaller sample.
key_finding: Biopsy-to-resection concordance was 92.5% at the 75% threshold, but sensitivity of biopsy for detecting positive tumors was only 54.6%, and lowering the biopsy threshold to 20% brought sensitivity to 100%. Recurrent lesions matched the primary in 83.3% of cases, with losses concentrated in local recurrence and liver metastasis.
caveats: The most decision-relevant row for the archival-versus-recurrence question here: expression usually persists at recurrence, but roughly one in six lesions diverges, and local recurrence is where loss clustered. Retrospective single-institution series.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 prevalence, primary-metastasis agreement, and neoadjuvant association in PDAC
model_system: 337 resected human PDAC cases with paired metastases (102 pairs), scored by IHC against the gastroesophageal trial criteria
mechanism: Prevalence and clinicopathologic correlation of CLDN18.2 staining, including relationship to prior neoadjuvant therapy.
key_finding: 280 of 337 cases (83.1%) had some staining and 90 (26.7%) met the trial-grade criterion of moderate-to-strong staining in at least 75% of cells. Primary and metastatic tissue agreed in 76.5% of pairs. Positive cases were less often ones that had received neoadjuvant chemoradiation, and among neoadjuvant-treated patients positivity carried a modest survival advantage (HR 0.66).
caveats: The neoadjuvant association is cross-sectional and cannot separate treatment-induced antigen loss from selection of tumors that were negative to begin with. It is still the closest available signal on whether chemotherapy erodes the antigen, which matters after ten FOLFIRINOX cycles.

intervention_label: satri-cel (CT041) — the hu8E5-2I CLDN18.2 CAR-T construct
journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
model_system: gastric cancer cell-line xenografts and CLDN18.2-positive PDX in mice
control_arm: untransduced T cells
mechanism: Second-generation CD28-costimulated CAR built on the humanized hu8E5-2I scFv — the same binder that underlies CT041/satri-cel.
key_finding: hu8E5-2I-28Z CAR-T suppressed xenograft growth (mean 75.5 mm3 versus 731.8 mm3 for untransduced T cells at day 29). Partial or complete tumor elimination occurred in CLDN18.2-positive PDX, with cells persisting and infiltrating tumor tissue.
caveats: Gastric models only. Mouse safety looked clean despite lysis of murine-CLDN18.2 targets, which did not predict the gastric mucosal injury later reported in patients.

intervention_label: AZD6422 (TGF-beta-armored CLDN18.2 CAR-T) — class mechanism for stromal suppression
model_system: patient-derived xenografts of gastric, esophageal and pancreatic tumors spanning a range of CLDN18.2 and TGF-beta levels
control_arm: conventionally manufactured CLDN18.2 CAR-T without TGF-beta armoring
mechanism: A CD28/CD3z CAR against CLDN18.2 carrying a dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor, so stromal TGF-beta cannot suppress the transferred cells; a shortened manufacturing process preserves potency.
key_finding: Antitumor activity held across PDX with varying antigen and TGF-beta levels, and the armoring advantage widened in high-TGF-beta tumors. Restimulation assays showed better persistence and cytolytic function than a conventionally manufactured product.
caveats: Immunodeficient PDX cannot report on the desmoplastic barrier or host immunity; TGF-beta armoring addresses one component of that barrier. AZD6422 itself is not among the trials screened for this case, so this is class evidence.

intervention_label: TAC01-CLDN18.2 (T-cell antigen coupler engineered T cells)
model_system: CLDN18.2-expressing gastric, gastroesophageal and pancreatic 2D cultures and spheroids; xenograft mice; primary human cells from vital organs
control_arm: non-transduced T cells; CLDN18.2-negative lines; normal-tissue cocultures
mechanism: The T-cell antigen coupler routes antigen recognition through the endogenous TCR complex rather than a synthetic signalling chain, which removes tonic signalling.
key_finding: Cytotoxicity tracked with CLDN18.2 level yet was still present in low-antigen models. Established xenografts were eradicated with durable responses on recursive killing and rechallenge, and no reactivity appeared against normal-tissue cells.
caveats: Sponsor preclinical package supporting the phase 1/2. Xenografts in immunodeficient mice leave stromal and host-immune barriers untested, and the clean normal-cell result sits uneasily beside the gastric toxicity seen with CAR constructs.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 STAR-T versus CAR-T in pancreatic cancer
model_system: pancreatic cancer models in vivo comparing CLDN18.2 STAR-T with CLDN18.2 CAR-T; gastroscopic assessment in treated patients
control_arm: CLDN18.2 CAR-T; untransduced T cells
mechanism: Synthetic TCR-and-antigen receptor signalling through the endogenous CD3 complex gives lower-gain activation than a second-generation CAR, trading potency for less normal-gastric damage; IL-12 p40 armoring recovers part of the potency.
key_finding: In vitro cytotoxicity matched CAR-T, but in vivo STAR-T caused less gastric damage and had weaker antitumor effect. Adding the IL-12beta p40 subunit improved STAR-T function in vitro and in mice.
caveats: The explicit potency-versus-gastric-toxicity trade is the honest framing for CLDN18.2 cell therapy in PDAC. The accompanying patient experience is small and uncontrolled.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 CAR-T on-target off-tumor gastric toxicity model
model_system: immunocompetent mouse model built on CLDN18.2 epitopes shared between human and mouse, dosed with CLDN18.2 CAR-T of varying design
control_arm: untransduced T cells; CAR variants differing in costimulatory domain; AND-gate logic constructs
mechanism: CAR-T recognize CLDN18.2 on normal gastric mucosa, and the resulting injury does not depend on construct design, costimulatory domain, or tumor model.
key_finding: The model reproduced gastric on-target off-tumor toxicity across constructs and served as a testbed for Boolean AND-gate mitigation. The authors caution that such models can overcall severity relative to patients as easily as undercall it.
caveats: Gastric toxicity is the practical dose ceiling for every CLDN18.2 cell therapy in this file. How it behaves in altered post-resection upper-GI anatomy is not modelled here.

intervention_label: Antigen-density threshold as a CAR design parameter
model_system: CD19- and GD2-directed CAR constructs tested against antigen-titrated tumor lines in vitro and in vivo
control_arm: parental CD19-4-1BBz and CD19-CD28z constructs; ITAM-deleted variants
mechanism: The antigen-density threshold for CAR activity is set by signal strength — ITAM count, hinge/transmembrane choice, costimulatory domain — rather than by the binder alone.
key_finding: CD28z CARs outperformed 4-1BBz CARs against antigen-low targets. Adding ITAMs or swapping a CD28 hinge/transmembrane into a 4-1BBz CAR lowered the recognition threshold while keeping the persistence advantage.
caveats: CD19 and GD2, not CLDN18.2, and no solid-tumor stroma. Included because construct design rather than the IHC percentage alone decides whether 2+/3+ staining in 60% of cells is enough antigen for a given product.

intervention_label: AZD5863 (CLDN18.2xCD3 affinity-modulated T-cell engager)
model_system: CLDN18.2-expressing human lines cocultured with human or cynomolgus PBMC; humanized and human-CD3 transgenic mice bearing pancreatic, gastric and esophageal tumors
control_arm: a CLDN18.2 engager with higher CD3 affinity; CLDN18.2-negative lines
mechanism: High CLDN18.2 affinity paired with deliberately low CD3 affinity preserves killing while cutting peripheral cytokine release; killing spreads to antigen-negative neighbours partly through IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha and Fas ligand.
key_finding: Potency correlated significantly with CLDN18.2 receptor density. Bystander killing of CLDN18.2-negative cells occurred whenever positive cells were present, and tumor control was achieved in pancreatic as well as gastric and esophageal models.
caveats: Density dependence cuts both ways for a tumor staining 2+/3+ in only 60% of cells — the bystander arm is why heterogeneity may still be tractable, but this is cell-line xenograft work without stroma-rich or organoid modelling.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2xCD3 engager class — T-cell-cold tumors and combination rescue
model_system: syngeneic solid-tumor models in huCD3e transgenic mice treated with mouse-CLDN18.2, mouse-CD19 and human-EPCAM BiTE molecules
control_arm: vehicle; CD8 and CD4 depletion arms; checkpoint blockade and 4-1BB agonism alone
mechanism: Redirected lysis depends on T cells already present in the tumor: efficacy comes from local CD8+ expansion rather than recruitment from the circulation, and CD4+ T cells antagonize the response.
key_finding: Pretreatment intratumoral T-cell density was the dominant determinant of BiTE response across models. In poorly infiltrated, immunotherapy-refractory tumors, adding checkpoint blockade or 4-1BB agonism restored activity.
caveats: Syngeneic models, none of them pancreatic. It is the cleanest mechanistic reason to expect a CLDN18.2 engager to underperform in a T-cell-poor MSS pancreatic tumor, and it names the combinations that fixed it in mice.

intervention_label: givastomig (TJ033721/ABL111, CLDN18.2x4-1BB bispecific)
model_system: gastric PDX-derived tumor cells with human PBMC; humanized 4-1BB transgenic mice bearing CLDN18.2-expressing tumors; cynomolgus toxicology; multiplex IHC of 60 gastric tumors
n_units: n=60 gastric tumors for the multiplex IHC arm
control_arm: parental anti-4-1BB agonist antibody; CLDN18.2-negative tumor cells
mechanism: 4-1BB agonism is conditional on CLDN18.2 engagement, so costimulation fires only where tumor antigen is present, avoiding the liver toxicity of systemic 4-1BB antibodies.
key_finding: The magnitude of T-cell activation tracked with CLDN18.2 level on PDX tumor cells while remaining detectable across a range of expression. In transgenic mice the antibody raised the intratumoral CD8/Treg ratio, controlled tumors, and produced memory on rechallenge; monkeys showed no systemic immune activation or hepatotoxicity.
caveats: Gastric models throughout, with no pancreatic arm. Conditional costimulation still needs T cells inside the tumor, which is exactly what a desmoplastic MSS PDAC tends not to supply.

intervention_label: AZD0901 / CMG901 (CLDN18.2 ADC, MMAE payload)
model_system: CLDN18.2-expressing tumor cell lines and cocultures; patient-derived xenografts; rat and cynomolgus toxicology
control_arm: isotype ADC; CLDN18.2-negative cells
dose_and_schedule: every-3-week dosing in toxicology; HNSTD 6 mg/kg (cynomolgus) and 10 mg/kg (rat)
mechanism: MMAE delivered on a CLDN18.2 antibody kills through direct cytotoxicity plus ADCC, CDC, and bystander killing of neighbouring cells.
key_finding: Binding was CLDN18.2-specific and killing ran through all four mechanisms in vitro, with significant antitumor activity in PDX. Toxicology was dominated by reversible MMAE-type hematopoietic effects.
caveats: PDX work is gastric-weighted with no separately reported pancreatic arm and no expression-threshold analysis, so the antigen level needed for activity is not pinned down here.

intervention_label: IBI343 (CLDN18.2 ADC, exatecan payload) — bystander-payload rationale, by class analogy
model_system: HER2-positive/HER2-negative cocultures; mixed NCI-N87 + MDA-MB-468-Luc xenografts imaged in vivo; contralateral-tumor control
control_arm: T-DM1 and an anti-HER2 ADC bearing a low-permeability payload
mechanism: A membrane-permeable topoisomerase-I payload (DXd, an exatecan derivative) diffuses out of the antigen-positive cell and kills antigen-negative neighbours; the low-permeability DM1 payload does not.
key_finding: DS-8201a killed both antigen-positive and antigen-negative cells in coculture and suppressed the antigen-negative population in mixed xenografts, while T-DM1 did not. The effect stayed local — a contralateral antigen-negative tumor was unaffected.
caveats: HER2 in breast and gastric models, not CLDN18.2 in pancreas. It is the mechanistic reason an exatecan-payload CLDN18.2 ADC could act on a tumor staining in 60% of cells, but the extrapolation crosses both target and tumor type and should not be read as tier-matched proof.

intervention_label: Desmoplastic barrier to drug delivery in PDAC (hyaluronan/IFP mechanism)
model_system: autochthonous KPC mouse PDA with direct interstitial fluid pressure measurement; PEGPH20 plus gemcitabine
control_arm: gemcitabine monotherapy; vehicle
mechanism: Hyaluronan generates gel-fluid pressure that collapses tumor vessels and obstructs perfusion, diffusion and convection of therapeutics; enzymatic HA removal normalizes pressure and re-expands the microvasculature.
key_finding: Interstitial fluid pressures in PDA exceeded prior measurements and theoretical estimates for solid tumors. PEGPH20 with gemcitabine remodeled the microenvironment durably, produced consistent objective responses, and nearly doubled overall survival versus gemcitabine alone.
caveats: The barrier mechanism is solid; the therapeutic translation failed, since PEGPH20 did not improve survival in the phase 3 HALO-301. Delivery is a real problem, but enzymatic HA depletion was not the answer.

intervention_label: Hyaluronan and macromolecular permeability in PDAC (bearing on antibodies, ADCs and engagers)
model_system: genetically engineered mouse model of PDA treated with PEGPH20, assessed for perfusion, vascular permeability and intratumoral drug delivery
control_arm: vehicle; gemcitabine monotherapy
mechanism: Depleting hyaluronan re-expands collapsed vessels and opens endothelial fenestrations and interendothelial gaps, so large molecules as well as small ones reach the tumor.
key_finding: PEGPH20 raised intratumoral delivery of doxorubicin and gemcitabine and produced a tumor-specific rise in macromolecular permeability. Combination with gemcitabine slowed tumor growth and prolonged survival over gemcitabine alone.
caveats: The macromolecular-permeability result is the part that speaks to antibody, ADC and engager penetration rather than small molecules. Same clinical caveat as Provenzano: the delivery mechanism never converted into survival benefit for PEGPH20.

intervention_label: Why checkpoint blockade fails in PDAC: FAP+ CAF-derived CXCL12 and T-cell exclusion
model_system: autochthonous KPC PDA mice; genetic depletion of FAP+ carcinoma-associated fibroblasts; AMD3100 plus anti-PD-L1
control_arm: anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 alone; untreated tumor-bearing mice
mechanism: FAP-expressing CAFs secrete CXCL12, which coats cancer cells and keeps T cells out of tumor regions; blocking CXCR4 releases that exclusion.
key_finding: Cancer-specific CD8+ T cells were present yet checkpoint blockade did nothing until FAP+ stromal cells were depleted. AMD3100 caused rapid T-cell accumulation among cancer cells and acted synergistically with anti-PD-L1, leaving mainly premalignant epithelium behind.
caveats: The mechanistic case that PDAC's checkpoint failure is exclusion, not absent antigen. CXCR4 combinations have not converted this into clinical benefit, and nothing surfaced for this case attacks the CXCL12 axis.

intervention_label: FAK-driven fibrosis and immunosuppression as the gate on checkpoint response in PDAC
model_system: p48-Cre;LSL-KrasG12D;Trp53flox/+ (KPC) mice treated with the FAK inhibitor VS-4718; human PDAC tissue for the FAK-fibrosis correlation
control_arm: vehicle; anti-PD-1 alone; adoptive T-cell therapy alone
mechanism: Hyperactive FAK in neoplastic cells sustains the fibrotic, myeloid-rich microenvironment that keeps CD8+ T cells out.
key_finding: FAK activity in human PDAC tracked with fibrosis and poor CD8+ infiltration. VS-4718 alone limited progression and doubled survival in KPC mice while cutting fibrosis and immunosuppressive infiltrate, and it made previously refractory tumors responsive to PD-1 blockade and T-cell therapy.
caveats: KPC carries Kras G12D with mutant Trp53, so the co-mutation shape resembles this case but the allele does not. FAK inhibitors have not reproduced this effect in PDAC trials.

intervention_label: Chemosensitivity is agent-specific in PDAC organoids (bearing on FOLFIRINOX-to-gemcitabine cross-resistance)
model_system: patient-derived PDAC organoid library with paired genomic, transcriptomic and drug profiling; matched patient outcomes
control_arm: untreated organoids; cross-agent comparison within the same organoid
mechanism: Response is organoid-intrinsic and drug-specific, with distinct transcriptomic signatures for 5-FU, irinotecan, oxaliplatin, gemcitabine and paclitaxel rather than one general chemosensitivity axis.
key_finding: Organoid drug profiles paralleled the matched patients' clinical courses, including longitudinal and synchronous-metastasis sampling. Per-agent signatures predicted response in independent adjuvant and advanced cohorts, and chemorefractory organoids were used to nominate targeted alternatives.
caveats: Separate per-drug signatures argue against assuming that FOLFIRINOX failure predicts gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel failure. The analysis is correlative and organoid pharmacotyping has never been validated prospectively for treatment selection.

intervention_label: Treatment-enriched malignant programs after neoadjuvant therapy in PDAC
model_system: 43 primary human PDAC specimens, treatment-naive or post-neoadjuvant, profiled by single-nucleus RNA-seq and whole-transcriptome spatial profiling
control_arm: treatment-naive specimens
mechanism: Chemotherapy and radiation shift the malignant compartment toward a neural-like progenitor program and reorganize spatial multicellular communities, rather than simply selecting a pre-existing subtype.
key_finding: The neural-like progenitor program was enriched after chemotherapy and radiotherapy and carried poor prognosis in independent cohorts. Three spatial communities emerged — classical, squamoid-basaloid, and treatment-enriched.
caveats: Descriptive human-tissue profiling with no therapeutic arm. It offers plausible biology for aggressive recurrence months after FOLFIRINOX but names no drug, and the neural-like program has no targeted agent.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 on-target/off-tumor toxicity modeling (Carstens)
exclusion_reason: Reaches the same conclusion as Birocchi (PMID 41176533) about gastric on-target injury from CLDN18.2-directed therapy; the Birocchi row was kept because it also tests AND-gate mitigation, and logging two overlapping models would double-count one mechanism.

intervention_label: satri-cel (CT041) response correlates by single-cell sequencing
exclusion_reason: Correlative single-cell analysis of blood and ascites from five patients already on a CAR-T trial, not a preclinical model; the naive-like-T-cell and CLDN18-high/MYC-high prognostic splits are hypothesis-generating at n=5.

intervention_label: CLDN18.2 expression in PDAC — systematic review and meta-analysis
exclusion_reason: Aggregate of published IHC series rather than primary model or specimen data; its decision-relevant point, that positivity varies significantly by antibody clone, is already carried by the primary concordance studies retained here.

intervention_label: KMT2C loss and ferroptosis sensitivity in meningioma
exclusion_reason: KMT2C-loss vulnerability reported in NF2-wild-type meningioma; neither the lineage nor the Hippo/ferroptosis axis has an established counterpart in PDAC, and no agent in the surfaced set acts on it.

intervention_label: MLL3 adaptor versus catalytic function in breast tumor suppression
exclusion_reason: Un-peer-reviewed preprint in breast models. Its argument that MLL3's adaptor rather than catalytic role drives tumor suppression would predict catalytic-site inhibitors are futile, which is worth knowing but too preliminary and too far from PDAC to enter the synthesis.

intervention_label: RAF1 S257L/S259F and intrinsic daraxonrasib resistance in melanoma
exclusion_reason: Melanoma models with no PDAC or KRAS G12R context, and RAF1 hotspot mutations do not appear on this patient's sequencing report.

intervention_label: Stereotactic radiotherapy combined with KRAS inhibition in PDAC
exclusion_reason: bioRxiv preprint pairing SBRT with KRAS inhibition; radiotherapy combination sits outside the modalities the trial screen surfaced for this case, and the work has not been peer reviewed.
